Alright! There it is, the next trade has arrived.

For me, it is time to take a long.

Long, you said Astro? What about the FOMC reversal, has it finished? What does that mean for our shorts?

Keep reading.

The type of long

It's an intraweek long, a long to complete the weekly move. That's still a swing trade, but it means all liquidity left during the week needs to be cleared.

Why a long? Why ignore the remainder of the FOMC reversal?

Yes FOMC reversal is still at play, and our 7% minimal drawdown still isn't finished.

But you have to keep in mind, that we called the FOMC reversal from 66.3k, where we entered short, and we already dropped 6.3%+ from the high.

If you think you can get away with just using 1 confluence all the time, and make money consistently, you will get wrecked instead.

Not always financially, but at the very least emotionally, which propagates into financial ruin regardless.

And that's because when a move starts to get close to completion, bounces against the move start to become more violent. That's again the trapping mechanism at work trapping big liquidity before reaching big liquidity.

So what's the move to finish the week? It's the untouched weekly open and the liquidity left during the course of the week.

That's almost a 2000 points move at least, lots of money to be made.

So what about our shorts?

It's simple, given the FOMC reversal is coming to an end for its initial move, it's no longer beneficial to hold the aggressive short (short IV). But it still makes sense to hold short III, because that's the top short, that's the one that should be closed only when most of the confluences fully confirm the FOMC reversal is over, not the case yet.

So in summary, the plan is simple:

➡️We have developed the bulk of the FOMC reversal move down
➡️The weekly move is still unfinished, likely to complete this week possibly all the way into next week.
➡️Close short VI, flip it into a long.

TLDR;
➡️Fully close aggressive short IV
➡️Flip into new long position
